unresolved_critical_dependencies.topic: duckdb#25824 is OPEN: silent value mutation past the sniffer sample
unresolved_critical_dependencies.state: Open as of capture (created 2026-09-17; updated 2026-09-24). No fix, no milestone in the captured JSON. If the workspace relied on sniffer-inferred schemas, this defect would silently corrupt large files; the design therefore forbids silently-trusted inferred schemas for contract-relevant reads.
unresolved_critical_dependencies.bounded_alternative: Product rule: preview/schema panels may use the sniffer; any replay-relevant read must carry an explicit columns/types contract or sample_size=-1 confirmation, and contract imports record which path was used.

unresolved_critical_dependencies.topic: Beyond-RAM performance on the 16 GB / 5 GB envelope
unresolved_critical_dependencies.state: Only a 0.9.0 feature announcement (S11, out-of-core hash aggregate storage) supports the claim that aggregation spills; no benchmark was run and no current-release memory_limit/temp_directory semantics were captured. The 5 GB streaming target remains a target, not a result.
unresolved_critical_dependencies.bounded_alternative: P1 witness; if spill behavior disappoints, the bounded alternative is chunked pandas/pyarrow processing for filter/project/aggregate ops with explicit refusal for global ops, keeping DuckDB only for SQL convenience on smaller data.

optional_opportunities.topic: SQL convenience path over the embedded engine
optional_opportunities.note: Expose DuckDB SQL against registered data refs as an optional transform cell type; record query text + engine version + ref versions as an execution event, so SQL results enter the same provenance graph instead of a separate tool. Rejected-as-requirement: full multi-language kernel support.
zip of project record + content-addressed data cache entries (DVC-style .dir manifests, S8) gives a single-file share; ordinary folders remain the primary exchange (brief requirement).
Large cell results as Arrow/Parquet pointers instead of inline mime bundles; noted, not investigated this stage.

optional_opportunities.topic: Content-defined chunking for faster re-hashing of large CSVs
optional_opportunities.note: Full-file sha256 of a 5 GB file costs seconds-to-minutes; head+tail+sparse-window approximate identity is the default, with exact hashing as an explicit background op. Alternative mechanism, UNVERIFIED here.
Explicitly out of scope per brief; the append-only event log is shaped so a future sync layer could replay it, but nothing in the minimum workflow depends on it.
